author: w. a. rice
title: Scott Hilton appointed to Emory University Board of Visitors for two-year term
text:
State Representative Scott Hilton (R-Peachtree Corners) has been appointed to a two-year term on Emory University’s Board of Visitors. The board, established in 1958, aims to foster connections between the university and the broader community by involving leaders from various sectors.
Hilton expressed his appreciation for the appointment, stating, “I’m honored to join the Emory Board of Visitors and look forward to engaging with the dynamic community of scholars and leaders. It’s a privilege to contribute to a tradition that values service, innovation and meaningful connection. I’m especially excited to learn from Emory’s thought leaders and explore ways to strengthen the relationship between higher education, community engagement and public policy to better serve the people of our state.”
The Board of Visitors is composed of executive leaders from corporate, public, and nonprofit backgrounds. Its goal is to connect these professionals with opportunities at Emory while encouraging participation beyond alumni circles. Less than one-third of current board members are alumni, which supports greater involvement from non-alumni.
Board members participate in meetings and presentations designed to introduce them to key initiatives at Emory. Many former members have continued their involvement with the university by serving on other boards or committees.
For more information about the Emory Board of Visitors, visit www.gca.emory.edu/board.
